input: This study set out to investigate the adsorption of a dye from water onto activated carbon, and a series of batch tests was carried out at a temperature of 298 K in order to explore the behaviour of the system. The experimental data were fitted to the Langmuir model, and the fitted Langmuir capacity was found to be 218 mg of dye per gram of adsorbent at pH 7, which represents the maximum capacity according to that particular model. In a further set of experiments, an adsorbent dose of 0.8 g L-1 was used, and after a contact time of 120 min the removal had reached 87% of the initial dye concentration, which was 50 mg L-1 at the start of the test. In that test, removal after 120 min reached 87% of the initial dye concentration of 50 mg L-1 at the adsorbent dose of 0.8 g L-1. The fitted capacity of 218 mg of dye per gram of adsorbent at pH 7 is the value that the Langmuir model approaches under those conditions. These results show that the activated carbon is quite effective at removing the dye under the conditions that were studied, and they provide a useful starting point for thinking about how the material might perform in a treatment process, where the contact between the water and the carbon would be arranged in a rather different way from a batch test and where the water itself would bring other substances with it. It should be noted, however, that the Langmuir fit is reported for pH 7 only, and the capacity at other pH values was not measured in this work, so the findings should be interpreted within that particular scope.
target: Adsorption of a dye from water on activated carbon was measured in batch tests at 298 K. The fitted Langmuir capacity was 218 mg of dye per gram of adsorbent at pH 7. At an adsorbent dose of 0.8 g L-1, removal after 120 min was 87% of the initial dye concentration of 50 mg L-1. The capacity figure and the removal figure describe different quantities. The Langmuir capacity is a fitted parameter of the isotherm at pH 7: it states the loading the fitted model approaches, and it comes from the fit rather than from a single measurement. The removal figure (87% after 120 min at a dose of 0.8 g L-1) is a measured outcome at one dose, one contact time and one initial concentration of 50 mg L-1. A change in any of those conditions changes the removal, and that percentage does not transfer to other doses or other starting concentrations. Scope is stated with the results: the Langmuir fit is reported for pH 7 only, and capacity at other pH values was not measured. Whether the same capacity holds away from that pH is therefore open, and the value of 218 mg per gram holds at that pH, not as a property of the carbon across pH. The two figures also have different standing as evidence. A fitted capacity depends on the model chosen for the fit and on the range of concentrations the fit was made over, neither of which is carried by the number itself; a measured removal depends on the arrangement of the test and on nothing else. A reader who takes the capacity as a measured loading, or the removal as a property of the carbon rather than of the test, reads both figures as more than they are.
